evals.prompt: Sandbox note: this environment has Python but no GPU, no CUDA driver and no network access, and torch may not be importable; do not install anything and do not try to execute the GPU code. Our manual full-step CUDA graph capture fails in three different ways. The relevant code is in /workspace/input/cudagraph-capture-errors/train_graph.py and the three failing runs are in /workspace/input/cudagraph-capture-errors/capture_errors.log. For each run, tell me which stream-capture error it is, the root cause, and the exact code change that fixes it.
evals.expected_output: Run 1 is cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated (901): the DataLoader pin_memory thread makes CUDA calls during global-mode capture; use capture_error_mode="thread_local" (or pin_memory=False / pin before capture). Run 2 is StreamCaptureImplicit (906): DDP/AccumulateGrad set up on the default stream; build DDP inside the side-stream context, warm up 11 iterations there and set TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=0. Run 3 is StreamCaptureUnjoined (904): the aux EMA stream is never joined back; add torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(aux) before the capture ends.
assertions: Run 1: identifies 'operation failed due to a previous error during capture' as cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated (901) caused by the DataLoader pin_memory background thread, and fixes it with torch.cuda.graph(..., capture_error_mode="thread_local") (or by disabling/avoiding pinned-memory allocation during capture).

Run 2: identifies 'operation would make the legacy stream depend on a capturing blocking stream' as StreamCaptureImplicit (906) caused by DDP/AccumulateGrad being set up on the default stream, and fixes it by constructing DDP inside the side-stream context and warming up there before capture.
For the DDP case, specifies 11 warmup iterations (instead of 3) and setting TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=0 before init_process_group.

Run 3: identifies 'capturing stream has unjoined work' as StreamCaptureUnjoined (904) caused by the aux EMA stream never rejoining, and fixes it with torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(aux) (capture stream waits on the side stream) before the capture block ends.
Does not attempt to run the script or install packages in the sandbox.

evals.prompt: We pretrain a GPT model with Megatron-LM (Megatron Core 0.14) using FP8 through Transformer Engine, pipeline parallel size 4 and tensor parallel size 2, with a fixed sequence length and micro-batch size. Nsight Systems shows kernel launch gaps between layers. We want the maximum speedup from CUDA Graphs. Which CUDA graph approach should we use, which exact flags do we need, and what in a typical training loop will break capture? Please answer from what you know; nothing needs to be run.
evals.expected_output: Use Megatron Core's FullCudaGraphWrapper for full-iteration capture: --enable-cuda-graph --cuda-graph-scope full_iteration --cuda-graph-warmup-steps 1 --te-rng-tracker --no-check-for-nan-in-loss-and-grad. TE RNG keeps RNG state in device tensors (the standard RNG uses CPU scalars), and the NaN check calls .item(), which is forbidden during capture. Forward+backward for all micro-batches becomes one graph (plus one for validation), the optimizer stays eager by default, and per-layer CudaGraphManager is the fallback.
assertions: Recommends Megatron Core's FullCudaGraphWrapper (full-iteration capture via --cuda-graph-scope full_iteration) as the maximum-performance option for this static workload.
Lists the enabling flags --enable-cuda-graph, --cuda-graph-scope full_iteration, a --cuda-graph-warmup-steps value, --te-rng-tracker and --no-check-for-nan-in-loss-and-grad.
Explains that --te-rng-tracker is required because the standard RNG uses CPU scalars that cannot be captured, whereas TE's RNG tracker keeps its state in device tensors.
Explains that --no-check-for-nan-in-loss-and-grad is required because the NaN check calls .item(), a host-device sync that is forbidden during capture.

Mentions per-layer CudaGraphManager (--enable-cuda-graph with --cuda-graph-num-warmup-steps) as the fallback if full-iteration capture is not feasible, with FP8 and pipeline-parallel interleaving handled automatically by the MCore APIs.
Notes that the optimizer step stays in eager mode by default and can optionally be moved inside the graph for extra performance.
